subject: Committed Capacity term, ramp, and start-window for Elkview (revised proposal)
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@elkview.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity commit questions and preferred start window

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Elkview's usage profile is shaping up faster than we projected. We ran a quick run-rate and attached a conservative MAU/token estimate for the first 12 months. Before we sign anything, two items we need clarified from your side:

1) Term flexibility: we prefer a 24-month committed path but want an option to convert the final 6 months to a month-to-month if usage drops below a threshold. Is that something Redwood supports in a written addendum?

2) Start-window: our current plan is to go live mid-Jan but procurement is pushing a Feb 1 start date. Can we align a ramp schedule that begins on Feb 1 but allows a Jan technical start (dry-run) without counting toward the committed units?

Also looping in Priya from procurement on schedule constraints. We're hopeful we can finalize this by end of November.

Appended: Elkview_MAU_and_tokens_estimate.xlsx (attachment, spreadsheet)

Regards,
Samir Rao
Head of Product
Elkview AI
From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@elkview.ai>, Priya Desai <priya@elkview.ai>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity commit questions and preferred start window

Samir — thanks for the estimate, that helps a lot. Quick answers up front:

• Term conversion: we can build a conditional convert clause for the final 6 months (24-month contract with the last 6 months opt-in to month-to-month) tied to a usage trigger. The trigger needs to be specific (e.g., sustained avg tokens/day below X for 60 days). We should get a draft clause from legal.

• Technical dry-run: yes — we do a zero-billing technical window commonly (dev and staging traffic routed to reserved infra but not billed against the commit). We call it a "pre-commit validation window" and can set it to Jan 15–Jan 31. Billing would begin Feb 1.

I'll have Dev (cc'd) build a ramp proposal with GPU pool sizing for the usage profile you sent and a few throughput SLO options (p50/p95 latency guarantees). Expect that doc tomorrow.

Next steps: I can send a revised PDF proposal including the clause language and a proposed ramp schedule; Priya, would procurement want this as a single PDF for review or separate SOW + T&Cs?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced in thread: Elkview_MAU_and_tokens_estimate.xlsx
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@elkview.ai>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Priya Desai <priya@elkview.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 10:31:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved commit ramp and sizing options (draft)

Hi all —

I pulled the numbers from Samir's estimate and sketched three conservative ramp plans for a 24-month commit. Key assumptions are in the first tab of the attached spreadsheet. High-level options:

Option A — Conservative ramp (lowest up-front commitment):
- Month 1–3: 25% of committed GPU pool (warm-up)
- Month 4–6: 50%
- Month 7 onward: 100%
- Throughput guarantee: baseline p95 token latency under 600ms (on 8xA100 pool)
- Notes: lower monthly cost; larger unit price due to slower ramp

Option B — Balanced ramp (recommended):
- Month 1–2: 40%
- Month 3–4: 75%
- Month 5 onward: 100%
- Throughput guarantee: p95 token latency under 450ms (on 12xA100 pool)
- Notes: better trade-off on unit economics vs. burst capacity

Option C — Aggressive ramp (fast scale):
- Month 1: 60%
- Month 2: 90%
- Month 3 onward: 100% + 15% burst buffer
- Throughput guarantee: p95 token latency under 350ms (on 16xA100 pool)
- Notes: best for UX-sensitive launches, requires higher committed spend

Term conversion clause idea (draft language):
"If average daily token consumption across any rolling 60-day window falls below 40% of committed tokens for months 19–24, Customer may elect to convert the final 6 months to month-to-month at a reduced rate equal to 120% of the committed per-month unit price."

Pre-commit validation: we can configure a Jan 15–31 validation window that routes traffic to your reserved pool without counting toward the committed usage. We'll provide monitoring dashboards and replay hooks to confirm readiness.

I've attached a PDF proposal with pricing tiers, discount ladders by committed GPU count, and sample SLOs. If you want, I can also produce per-region sizing (we assume US-west primary).

Attachments: Redwood_Reserved_Commit_Proposal_ELK-2026.pdf (proposal)

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Desai <priya@elkview.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity commit questions and preferred start window

Tessa / Dev — thanks for the clear options. Procurement preference is Option B (balanced ramp) with the term-conversion clause included, subject to one change: the conversion trigger should allow a 90-day cure window for usage dips (i.e., if the trigger trips, Customer can restore usage above threshold within 90 days to avoid conversion). Also would like the final SOW to call out a one-time onboarding credit if the technical dry-run requires extra engineering time.

Priya Desai
Head of Procurement
Elkview AI
